title: U.S. Senate · Arkansas

context.text: This is a regularly scheduled election for the Class II Senate seat held by incumbent Tom Cotton (R), who first took office in 2015. Cotton defeated Micah Ashby and Jeb Little 81.6%-9.2%-9.1% in the March 3, 2026 Republican primary. Hallie Shoffner defeated Ethan Dunbar 78.3%-21.7% in the Democratic primary; Dan Whitfield and James Russell withdrew from that primary before the vote. Jeff Wadlin advanced as the Libertarian Party nominee from a February 22, 2026 party convention.

summary.text: Tom Cotton is the Republican nominee and incumbent U.S. Senator from Arkansas, seeking a third term. A Harvard-educated lawyer and Army infantry officer who served in Iraq and Afghanistan, he worked as a management consultant, served one term in the U.S. House, and has been in the Senate since 2015, where he chairs the Select Committee on Intelligence and the Senate Republican Conference.

background.text: Born in Dardanelle, Arkansas, in 1977. According to his official Senate biography, he grew up on his family's cattle farm in Yell County and graduated from Dardanelle High School.
Earned a bachelor's degree in government from Harvard University in 1998 and a J.D. from Harvard Law School in 2002.
Worked as a law clerk for the U.S. Court of Appeals and in private law practice before leaving the law after the September 11 attacks to join the Army, according to his official biography.

Served nearly five years on active duty in the U.S. Army (2004-2009) as an infantry officer, including combat tours in Iraq with the 101st Airborne and in Afghanistan with a Provincial Reconstruction Team, and service with The Old Guard at Arlington National Cemetery. His decorations include the Bronze Star Medal, the Combat Infantryman Badge and the Ranger Tab.
Worked for McKinsey & Co. as a management consultant and, per Ballotpedia, also as a farmer, between leaving the Army and entering Congress.
Served one term in the U.S. House of Representatives for Arkansas's 4th District (2013-2015).
Was elected to the U.S. Senate in 2014, defeating incumbent Democrat Mark Pryor, and was re-elected in 2020 over Ricky Dale Harrington Jr.

In the Senate he serves on the Armed Services Committee, the Energy and Natural Resources Committee, and the Joint Economic Committee, and chairs the Select Committee on Intelligence. He is also Chairman of the Senate Republican Conference, the third-ranking position in Senate Republican leadership.
According to his official biography, he and his wife Anna have two sons, Gabriel and Daniel.

record.text: Currently chairs the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence and sits on the Committee on Armed Services (Subcommittees on Airland, Cybersecurity, Emerging Threats and Capabilities, and Strategic Forces), the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources, and the Joint Economic Committee.

summary.text: Hallie Shoffner is the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate in Arkansas. Describing herself as a sixth-generation Arkansas farmer and small-business owner, she ran the family farm in the Arkansas Delta for nine years before closing it to run for office. She is running on lowering costs for working families, protecting Social Security and Medicare, and strengthening health care and labor protections.

background.text: According to her campaign website, she grew up in Shoffner, a small farming community in the Arkansas Delta, raised in the fields alongside her farmer parents and learning to grow soybeans, rice, corn, cotton and wheat. She describes herself as a sixth-generation Arkansas farmer.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Vanderbilt University and a Master of Public Service from the University of Arkansas Clinton School of Public Service.

Operated the family farm for nine years, according to her campaign website, and has worked in conservation, sustainable farming and regional food production. She says she closed the farm after a year of rising costs, poor markets, new tariffs and no Farm Bill relief, to protect her parents' land and retirement.
Her campaign website describes her as a Presidential Leadership Scholar and a board member of the Arkansas Foodbank, and says she "didn't plan to run for office" and is "not a politician."
Won the Democratic primary for U.S. Senate on March 3, 2026, defeating Ethan Dunbar 78.3% to 21.7%.

priorities.text: Lower the cost of living for working families, including groceries, childcare, housing, and healthcare; raise the minimum wage.
Protect and strengthen Social Security and Medicare, including lifting the payroll-tax contribution cap on high earners.
Make healthcare more affordable by strengthening the Affordable Care Act, lowering prescription drug prices, and protecting Medicaid.
Support unions and workers' right to organize and bargain collectively.
Support Arkansas farmers and rural communities through regional food systems and a farm bill that expands market access.

positions.summary: Says she will fight to strengthen the Affordable Care Act, protect Medicare and Medicaid, and lower prescription drug prices.
positions.quote: I will fight to protect our hospitals, lower prescription drug prices, strengthen the Affordable Care Act, protect Medicare and Medicaid, cut red tape, and hold insurance companies accountable.

positions.summary: Campaign platform calls for raising the minimum wage as part of an "Arkansas-first economic plan."
positions.quote: That means raising the minimum wage, expanding workforce training, cutting taxes for working families, giving local businesses the resources they need to thrive, cutting red tape, and modernizing infrastructure.

positions.summary: Says she would lift the Social Security payroll-tax contribution cap on the "ultra wealthy" and opposes tax cuts she says benefited billionaires.
positions.quote: I will protect and strengthen Social Security and Medicare, lift the contribution cap on the ultra wealthy, reverse the cuts, and invest in a care economy that creates good-paying jobs and keeps seniors close to home.

candidates.name: Jeff Wadlin
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Libertarian Party's February 22, 2026 state convention.

summary.text: Jeff Wadlin is the Libertarian Party nominee for U.S. Senate in Arkansas. According to his campaign website, he is an engineer and businessman from Bentonville with an MBA who has worked at Caterpillar, Capital One and Sam's Club and now runs a consulting business. He says he is running because he is worried about where the country is headed and wants government to leave people alone unless they are harming someone else.

background.text: Says on his campaign website that he was born in Richmond, Virginia, moved around Illinois, Arizona and North Carolina, and chose to settle in Bentonville, Arkansas, where he is raising three sons.
Says he studied aerospace and mechanical engineering at the University of Virginia and earned an MBA from Northwestern.

Describes a career that includes working for Caterpillar, co-founding an Illinois online salvage yard for auto parts, working at Capital One's headquarters in Virginia, launching a product development company, running membership nationwide at Sam's Club in Bentonville, and founding his own consulting business.
Says he previously ran for Justice of the Peace and City Council and sought the Libertarian nomination for U.S. House in 2018 without winning.
Advanced from the Libertarian Party of Arkansas convention for U.S. Senate on February 22, 2026.

candidates.researchNotes: No detailed biography, stated policy positions, or Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey responses were found for Wadlin beyond his convention nomination and FEC filing.
